support.generic.help: Map typed in by a user; no claim about a specific device.
support.documented.help: Taken from a named manual revision and checked statically; not yet tested on hardware.
support.simulated.help: Works against the built-in simulator only. This is not hardware evidence.
support.hardware_verified.help: A recorded passing test on real hardware (model, firmware, adapter, platform).
alarm.banner.label: Alarm summary: open the alarm list
alarm.intro: Process alarms watch values against limits. Communication alarms watch data quality, one per device; while quality is bad, process alarms of that tag hold their state instead of flooding.
alarm.comm_note: Raised automatically when a device answers with TIMEOUT, CRC, exception, decode error, stale data or disconnect.
alarm.none.process: No process alarms defined. Add one below.
alarm.form.title: Add a process alarm
alarm.form.deadband.hint: Hysteresis: the value must move this far back inside the limit to clear.
alarm.form.latch: Latching: stays unacknowledged after it clears
alarm.form.defaults_note: Default deadband and delays follow ISA-18.2 practice: temperature 1 % of range and 60 s, pressure 2 %, flow/level 5 % and 15 s.
alarm.err.limit: Enter the limit as a number.
alarm.log.empty: No alarm events in this session yet.
connect.training.text: No hardware needed: starts a simulated RS485 bus with a soil sensor, a VFD and a temperature controller, all labeled as simulated.
connect.training.started: Training mode running: three simulated devices are polling.
connect.ports.none: No serial ports found. Plug in the USB-RS485 adapter, then refresh.
connect.isolation: The Waveshare USB TO RS485 (B) adapter is not isolated. For field work use an isolated adapter and wire GND between the adapter and the device.
connect.tcp.kind.hint: RTU over TCP sends raw RTU frames with CRC through a transparent serial server; it is not Modbus TCP.
connect.tcp.wifi: On Wi-Fi, client isolation on the access point can block the connection.
connect.connected: Link {id} connected. Add a device from the library, then start polling.
connect.err.baud: Baud must be a whole number from 300 to 3 000 000.
connect.err.host: Enter an IP address or host name.
connect.links.none: No links yet. Start Training mode or connect a port.
connect.links.no_devices: No devices on this link yet. Add one from the device library.
device.name: Device
library.intro: Profiles describe one device model. The same profile file is used on Windows and Android. Read support does not imply write support.
library.no_link: Connect a link first (or start Training mode) to add this device.
library.unit.hint: 1–247 on serial lines, 1–255 on TCP. 0 is broadcast and never allowed.
library.err.unit_number: Unit ID must be a whole number.
library.err.unit_zero: Unit ID 0 is broadcast and cannot be a device.
library.err.unit_range: Unit ID must be 1 to {max} on this link.
library.err.poll: Poll interval must be 100 ms to 24 h.
dash.paused: Paused: the values on screen are not live. Polling and logging continue.
tile.bar: Analog bar from {min} to {max}; shaded band is the normal range, ticks are alarm limits
export.title: Log and export
export.hint: Exports include quality, exception code, data age and profile version; times in ISO-8601 UTC, decimals with a dot.
trend.help: Lines break wherever data is not GOOD or missing; hatched bands mark the gap and its reason. Drag across the chart to zoom.
trend.decimated: Decimated: min/max per pixel (Rust side); spikes are kept
trend.raw_live: Raw samples from the live buffer
inspector.caption: Registers as read: the PDU offset is what goes on the wire; the doc address is the manual label.
inspector.address_note: Doc addresses in brackets are conventional labels (e.g. 40001 = holding register offset 0) because the profile has no manual label. BusLink never sends a label as an address.
exc.hint.01: The device does not support this function code.
exc.hint.02: Address not mapped on the device: check the address base (40001 vs offset 0) and the register map.
exc.hint.03: Quantity or value rejected: read fewer registers or check the value range.
exc.hint.04: The device reported an internal failure.
exc.hint.05: Long operation acknowledged; poll again later.
exc.hint.08: Memory parity error in the device.
exc.hint.0A: Gateway has no path to the target: check the gateway configuration.
exc.hint.0B: Gateway target did not respond: check the unit ID and wiring behind the gateway.
train.intro: Training mode runs a simulated RS485 bus inside the app. Inject faults to see how BusLink shows them: values keep their last good reading with its age, trends break at gaps, and communication alarms stay separate from process alarms.
train.faults.note: Faults act only on the simulator and end by themselves after the stated time.
train.unit.4: Unit 4: energy meter (simulated, add it from the library)
train.ex.read.title: 1. Read three devices
train.ex.read.steps: Start Training mode, open Overview and find the soil temperature, the VFD output frequency and the controller PV. Note the unit, quality and age on each tile.
train.ex.read.learn: Every value carries its quality and age; normal values have no color.
train.ex.timeout.title: 2. Recognise a timeout gap
train.ex.timeout.steps: Open Trends for the temperature controller, then inject Timeout on unit 3. Watch the tiles show TIMEOUT with the last value struck through and the trend break with a hatched “No data: TIMEOUT” band.
train.ex.timeout.learn: A lost reply never becomes 0 or a fresh value; other devices keep polling.
train.ex.order.title: 3. Word order check
train.ex.order.steps: Add the energy meter (unit 4) from the library. Inject Wrong word order and compare the four orders in the register inspector for voltage.
train.ex.order.learn: Choose the order from the manual, not from the value that looks plausible.
train.ex.stale.title: 4. Frozen data
train.ex.stale.steps: Inject Frozen values on unit 1. Replies stay GOOD but the values stop changing: this is a gateway serving a cache. Then stop polling on the link and watch the tiles turn STALE by age.
train.ex.stale.learn: GOOD quality is about the reply, not about the process; age tells you how old a value is.
train.ex.alarm.title: 5. Acknowledge and shelve
train.ex.alarm.steps: Inject Timeout on unit 2 and open Alarms: one communication alarm appears, process alarms of that device are held. Acknowledge it, then shelve a process alarm for 15 min and see it leave the banner count.
train.ex.alarm.learn: Acknowledged is not cleared; shelving is logged and expires.
train.ex.export.title: 6. Export a record
train.ex.export.steps: On Overview, export CSV and XLSX. Open the file and find the TIMEOUT rows with quality, exception code and age columns.
train.ex.export.learn: The record shows what was measured and what was not.
